1	# G5 residual: status consumers now read through the wrapper (source change, tests UNRUN). 2026-11-01
2	
3	Codex assigned this bounded phase under explicit owner delegation AUTH-01. A local Claude goal-implementer wrote it,
4	limited to Read, Grep, Edit and Write. It ran nothing: no process, test, CLI, database, network, environment or credential
5	read, and no commit. This record claims no Done-when box, no acceptance-ledger result, no whole-G5 closure and no MB-1
6	acceptance. It covers one named residual from `harness-command-failure-accepted-2026-11-01.md`.
7	
8	## Why
9	
10	QA-9 phase 3N gap G5 says status diagnostics can expose keys, and PRD 22.1 says never log tokens. The accepted F4
11	prerequisite moved the three integration suites onto `readLocalStatus` in `status-command.mjs`. That wrapper drops the
12	thrown value of a failed command without binding it, throws one fixed message, and parses through `parseStatusOutput`,
13	which has fixed refusals. Two consumers still ran `pnpm exec supabase status -o json` and parsed it inline:
14	
15	- `scripts/backend/environment.mjs` (`pnpm backend:env`) writes the mobile app's private `apps/mobile/.env.local`.
16	- `scripts/backend/preview-account.mjs` creates a synthetic local account and writes its credentials privately to tmpdir.
17	
18	In both, a failed command could throw Node's child-process error, which carries the printed output (keys) in its message,
19	`stdout` and `output`. Bad output could throw a V8 `SyntaxError` that quotes the input. With no handler, either one would
20	print to the terminal.
21	
22	## What changed
23	
24	Two lines changed in each consumer, each in place, so the line count and every line number stay the same:
25	
26	| File | Line | Before | After |
27	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
28	| `scripts/backend/environment.mjs` | 1 | `import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';` | `import { readLocalStatus } from './status-command.mjs';` |
29	| `scripts/backend/environment.mjs` | 3 | `const status = JSON.parse(execFileSync('pnpm', [...status -o json], {...}));` | `const status = readLocalStatus();` |
30	| `scripts/backend/preview-account.mjs` | 2 | `import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';` | `import { readLocalStatus } from './status-command.mjs';` |
31	| `scripts/backend/preview-account.mjs` | 7 | `const status = JSON.parse(execFileSync('pnpm', [...status -o json], {...}));` | `const status = readLocalStatus();` |
32	
33	Nothing else changed: not the exact loopback guard, not environment's `sb_publishable_` guard, not the file paths, modes
34	(`0o600`), messages, `randomUUID` IDs, fetch calls, apikey/secret handling or the tmpdir credential file. Both files
35	still have no other imports to touch, so there was no cleanup. The wrapper runs the same command, arguments and options
36	as before, so the success path is unchanged; `status-command.test.mjs` already covers that. Only the failure surface
37	changed: it now raises the wrapper's fixed messages. The wrapper also refuses JSON that is not an object; before, a JSON
38	`null` would have thrown a `TypeError` with no key in it.
39	
40	`docs/architecture/003-architecture-freeze.md` cites `environment.mjs:4-5`, which still points at the guard and the write.
41	
42	## Regression test (written first, UNRUN)
43	
44	New `scripts/backend/status-consumers.test.mjs`, pure `node:test`. It imports only `node:assert/strict`, `node:fs` and
45	`node:test`. It reads both consumers as text through `readFileSync`, never loads either one (they have real side
46	effects), has no run-time load, starts no process and makes no network call. Its four tests:
47	
48	1. **Exact scoped change.** The before-source is pinned as explicit per-line strings, copied from the out-of-repo snapshot
49	   `/tmp/fitlog-mb1-status-consumers-before.json`. Each consumer must equal that source with the child import replaced by
50	   the wrapper import and the inline parse replaced by `const status = readLocalStatus();`, and nothing else. The test
51	   also checks that only those two line indexes differ.
52	2. **Wrapper only.** Each consumer has one wrapper import line, one no-argument call, and `readLocalStatus` named exactly
53	   twice. Its static import list is exact and in order. No `child_process`, exec/spawn/fork call, `JSON.parse`, status
54	   command text, direct helper import, run-time load or `require` remains.
55	3. **Guard and body.** Only imports come before the status read. The existing exact guard follows it on the next line,
56	   unchanged, and appears once. The pinned guard contains the exact loopback check, plus the publishable-key check for
57	   environment. Everything after the guard matches the before-source byte for byte. Every listed side effect (writes,
58	   modes, logs, `randomUUID()`, `fetch(`, secret-key header, tmpdir file) appears after the guard and never before it.
59	4. **Self-check.** The test file's own static imports are exactly the three above, and it contains no run-time load.
60	
61	TDD order: the test was written before either consumer was edited. Expected against the before-source, by reading only:
62	tests 1–3 fail and test 4 passes. Expected after the change: 4/4 pass. Neither result was observed, because nothing was run.
63	
64	The proposed future command needs separate authorization. It is pure, uses no process, network or database, and loads
65	neither consumer:
66	
67	```
68	node --test scripts/backend/status-consumers.test.mjs
69	```
70	
71	The repository's usual prefix gives `rtk proxy node --test scripts/backend/status-consumers.test.mjs`. The
72	`backend:test` script's `scripts/backend/*.test.mjs` glob will also pick the file up, but that script goes on to run the
73	live suites, so it is not the proposed command.
74	
75	## Unchanged by design
76	
77	`status-command.mjs`, `status-output.mjs`, `status-command.test.mjs` and `status-output.test.mjs` were read only. They
78	should still match the reviewed SHA256 values in `harness-command-failure-accepted-2026-11-01.md`. No hashes were
79	computed this phase because no execution tool was available, so the verifier should record them. The snapshot was read,
80	not written.
81	
82	## Residual owners (open)
83	
84	- **MB-1 / QA-9 G5:** triage the `verify-freeze-projection.mjs` raw child-process and parse diagnostics. These were
85	  already named and are untouched here.
86	- **MB-1 / QA-9 G5:** in `preview-account.mjs`, `response.json()` and `login.json()` could throw a V8 `SyntaxError` that
87	  quotes part of a local auth response that isn't JSON. Token-bearing success bodies are valid JSON, so exposure is
88	  unlikely. This is out of scope for this phase, which allows no other security changes. It is named for triage.
89	- **MB-1 / QA-9:** G1–G4, G6, G7 (cleanup, timeout, target binding and the others), F1–F3, F5, F6, the allowlisted
90	  executor, exact shared-target binding, backend isolation suites and the whole of MB-1 stay open. Historical denied
91	  sequences stay parked.
92	
93	## Self-review (C/H/M/L)
94	
95	The `code-reviewer`, `security-reviewer` and `tdd-guide` sub-agents were not used: this phase's tool scope forbids
96	subagents.
97	
98	- **Critical:** none.
99	- **High:** none.
100	- **M1:** no independent review yet. An independent verifier must cover the code, security and TDD review.
101	- **M2:** the tests have not been run. The fixture strings were checked against the snapshot by hand only, including the
102	  `’` apostrophe, the escaped `\\n` inside the template text, and `${…}` written literally in plain strings. A
103	  fixture typo would give a false failure, not a false pass, because test 1 compares the whole file.
104	- **L1:** test 3's body check overlaps test 1, on purpose, so failures name the cause.
105	- **L2:** the checks are lexical and do not parse the JavaScript. Mistakes fail closed, and the whole-file pin is the
106	  strong check.
107	- **L3:** the self-check cannot rule out use of the global `fetch`, because the fixture strings contain `fetch(`.
108	  Reading the file shows no call.
109	- **L4:** the consumers now refuse JSON that is not an object with the helper's fixed message. This is stricter and
110	  intended.
111	- **L5:** the `response.json()` residual above.
112	- **L6:** `${…}` written literally in plain strings would trip `no-template-curly-in-string` if `scripts/backend` were
113	  ever linted. Today ESLint covers only `apps/mobile`.

1476	### 22.1 Access and information protection
1477	
1478	TLS in transit, encrypted managed storage/database/backups, secrets only server-side, scoped sessions
1479	and short-lived private URLs. Signed asset URL default five minutes, upload URL ten minutes, bound
1480	to owned object/size/type; issuance rechecks access. No permanent public progress/food/receipt URLs.
1481	Use authorized proxy or revocable access where immediate revocation is required; staff never receive
1482	URLs for personal health assets. Future passport links are independently revocable. Lock-screen notifications carry generic copy + safe destination ID.
1483	
1484	Enforce user ownership and tenant/operational-permission policies on every endpoint, worker and download.
1485	Route inventory isolation tests include filters, guessed IDs, exports, assets and jobs. Staff role
1486	cache cannot extend revoked permission. Audit gym finance, consent, roles, export, support access and
1487	sensitive reads. Access/audit logs retained at least one year, with payload minimization; never log
1488	OTP, token, raw AI input, photos, health values or location. Audit access itself is restricted.
